name: Hook strength
measures: How likely the first line is to earn the next three seconds: short, front-loaded, concrete, with tension or a gap, aimed at a recognisable viewer.
limitations: Reads text only. Delivery, the first frame and the on-screen visual decide as much as the words.
Rewards patterns that tend to work; it cannot predict reach, which depends on the audience and distribution.
Tension and specificity are detected from word lists and numbers, so a clever hook in plain words can score lower than it deserves.

criteria.label: Brevity
criteria.measures: Fits in roughly 2-3 seconds of speech.

rules.why: 5-14 words says it inside about three seconds.
rules.fix: Cut to the noun, the verb and the stake.

criteria.label: Front-loaded
criteria.measures: The point arrives in the first words, not after a warm-up.

rules.why: Greetings spend the only seconds you have.
rules.fix: Delete the greeting; start on the claim.
Start on the most specific word.

rules.why: Concrete details make a claim believable and visual.
rules.fix: Add the number, the object or the exact situation.

rules.why: Numbers stop thumbs. Only use true ones.

criteria.label: Tension or gap
criteria.measures: A conflict, a cost, or an open question the viewer wants closed.

rules.why: Conflict (wrong, cost, stop, nobody) or a gap (why, the real reason, what happens) gives a reason to keep watching.
rules.fix: Name what is at stake, what is wrong, or open a question the next line answers.

rules.why: 'You' puts the viewer in the line.
Uses the audience's own words from the creator profile.
rules.fix: Name the audience or their situation in their words.

criteria.label: Known formula
criteria.measures: Matches a formula from the hook library.

rules.why: A recognised shape is easier to judge and to iterate on. Off-formula is allowed.

criteria.label: Clean language
criteria.measures: No AI-sounding filler or template phrasing.

rules.why: Slop words read as generated and make the line vaguer.
rules.fix: Replace the flagged word with the concrete thing.

rules.why: Template constructions ('here's the thing', 'not just X but Y') announce instead of saying.
rules.fix: Cut the announcement; say the thing.

dealbreakers.message: Opens with a greeting. Nobody opens Instagram to be greeted.
Begs for attention ('stop scrolling', 'wait for it'). Earn it instead.
Over 30 words. That is a paragraph, not a hook.
Over 20 words: too long to land in about three seconds.
Two or more slop terms in one line.
Uses a word the creator never uses (profile).
